steps.d: Check you qualify: you bought or acquired Everbridge (EVBG) common stock between February 18, 2020 and February 24, 2022. The deadline is November 25, 2026, so do this today.

Log in to your brokerage and download the trade confirmations or account statements that show every EVBG buy and sell from February 2020 through May 2022, plus how many shares you held on February 17, 2020 and on May 25, 2022.
Open https://veritaconnect.com/EverbridgeSecuritiesSettlement/ (linked from www.everbridgesecuritiessettlement.com) and start a new claim. File one claim per brokerage account.

Enter the claimant details: your name exactly as it appears on the account, any joint owner, your mailing address, phone and email, and the last 4 digits of your Social Security number (or your full TIN for an entity).
Enter your starting position: the number of EVBG shares you held at the close of February 17, 2020 (enter 0 if none).
Enter each purchase during the period: trade date, number of shares, price per share and total cost. Then enter each sale the same way, with proceeds.
Enter your ending position: the shares you still held on May 25, 2022.
Upload your brokerage statements or trade confirmations as PDFs or images so the administrator can verify every line.
Review the release and certification, then sign electronically. If the account is joint, the other owner must also sign.
Submit and save the confirmation page or claim number. Then paste that confirmation number into your Claimclub dashboard so we can track the payout (about $2.32 per eligible share, estimated).

If your shares came from the USBTC merger, find the merger exchange record from November 30, 2023.

Create your claimant account or start a new claim and enter your name, address, email, and phone, exactly as they appear on your brokerage account.

Enter how many Hut 8 shares you received in exchange for USBTC stock, and how many you received for Legacy Hut securities, if any.

Upload the brokerage statements or trade confirmations that back up every line you entered. Claims without records can be rejected.
Enter your payment details as the portal asks.
Read the release and certification, then sign electronically and submit before 11:59 p.m. EST on December 5, 2026 (or mail the signed paper form postmarked by then).
Save or screenshot the confirmation page and claim number.
Send that confirmation number to Claimclub from your dashboard so we can track it. If your broker offers to file for you, that is fine too, just tell us.

steps.d: Before you start, log in to your brokerage and download statements or trade confirmations showing your Big Rock Partners (BRPA) Class A shares held on June 8, 2021, every BRPA or NRXP trade from then through April 2, 2024, and your NRXP balance on April 2, 2024. The online form does not save progress, so have these ready.
If your broker holds your shares and offers to file claims for clients, you can ask them to file for you instead. If they do, skip the rest and tell Claimclub.
Open https://www.brpastockholdersettlement.com/Home/SubmitClaim in your browser.
Enter your name exactly as it appears on your brokerage account, plus your mailing address, email and phone number. If you have a notice with a claim ID, enter it, otherwise leave it blank.
Enter the last four digits of your Social Security number (or taxpayer ID) and your brokerage account number.
Enter the number of BRPA Class A shares you held at the close of trading on June 8, 2021. These are the shares you did not redeem before the merger.
Add every purchase and sale of BRPA or NRXP stock from after June 8, 2021 through April 2, 2024, with the date, number of shares and price for each trade.
Enter how many NRXP shares you still held at the close of trading on April 2, 2024. Enter 0 if you sold them all.
Upload your brokerage statements or trade confirmations as PDFs or clear photos. Black out unrelated account details if you like.
Read the certification, check the box and type your full name as your signature, then submit.
Save or screenshot the confirmation page and claim number, then send that confirmation number to Claimclub from your dashboard.

steps.d: Check you qualify: you bought Edwards Lifesciences (EW) common stock between February 6, 2024 and July 24, 2024. Claims are due December 2, 2026.

Gather your records first: log in to your brokerage and download statements or trade confirmations showing your EW shares held on February 6, 2024, every EW purchase and sale from February 6 to October 22, 2024, and your EW shares held on October 22, 2024.

Go to the official site, www.EdwardsLifesciencesSecuritiesLitigation.com, run by Kroll, and choose to submit a claim online. You can also print the Proof of Claim form and mail it. Never pay anyone to file.

Part I, Claimant Information: enter the account owner's name exactly as on the brokerage account, any joint owner, the last 4 digits of your Social Security number, your address, phone numbers and email, and pick the owner type (Individual for most people, or IRA if the shares were in an IRA).
File one claim per account. If you held EW in both a regular account and an IRA, submit a separate claim for each.
Part III, holdings: enter how many EW shares you held at the start of February 6, 2024 (enter 0 if none).
Part III, purchases: list every EW purchase from February 6 to October 22, 2024 with the trade date, number of shares, price per share and total cost.
Part III, sales: list every EW sale in the same period with date, shares, price and total, or check the box for none. Then enter the shares you held on October 22, 2024.
Upload (or attach copies of) your brokerage statements or confirmations for every line. Do not highlight anything and do not send originals.
Part IV: read the release and certifications, then sign and date as the account owner. Joint owners must both sign.
Submit, and save the confirmation page or number. Kroll sends an acknowledgement within 60 days. If you mailed it, keep a copy and use tracking to PO Box 5014, New York, NY 10150-5014.
Send your confirmation number to Claimclub from your dashboard so we can track your payout (estimated about $0.66 per share). Questions: 1-833-930-0555.

steps.d: Check you qualify: your NYC TLC license was suspended after an arrest between 2003 and 2020. Payments range from about $263 to $36,000 depending on how long you were suspended. Claims are due December 28, 2026.

Find the notice you got about the settlement. It has your Claim Login ID and PIN for filing online. If you lost it, contact the administrator (833-296-0847, info@TLCSuspensionClaims.com) with your full name and mailing address, or use the paper form, which needs no code.
Have ready your TLC license number (if you know it), your date of birth, and your Social Security number for the tax form.
Go to https://tlcsuspensionclaims.com/ and choose to file a claim online, then enter your Claim Login ID and PIN.
Confirm your name, mailing address, phone and email. Use an address where you reliably get mail.
Enter your TLC license number and date of birth.

Read the affirmation: it asks you to confirm that if a fair hearing had been offered after your suspension, you would have asked for one and believe in good faith you would have won. Confirm it only if true.
Sign the claim form yourself. Do not pay anyone who offers to file this for you; filing is free.
Complete and sign the City of New York Substitute Form W-9 with your Social Security number. The settlement cannot pay you without it, and the administrator may ask for it after final approval.
If you use the paper form instead, sign it and send it by mail (P.O. Box 25226, Santa Ana, CA 92799), fax ((714) 824-8591) or email (info@TLCSuspensionClaims.com) by December 28, 2026.
Save the confirmation page or number, and keep a copy of anything you sent.
Send that confirmation number to Claimclub from your dashboard so we can follow up on your payment.
